description: how we can help atronauts go further into space
summary: Astrospectra: Rad-Sentry is an autonomous cosmic ray early-warning and crew-defense system designed to protect astronauts during deep space missions. By integrating live space weather telemetry from NASA's DONKI API with ultra fast optical  particle sensor NASA'S SNSPD. It is important because this app and the chambers will help an astronaut go further into deep space and explore other planets without the danger of cosmic rays, radiations etc. since these situations might cause the astronauts very bad harms since these radiations are very common in space; We shall be able to send our astronauts without the fear of them nearly dying while exploring planets.
details: This app has an automated crew defense which tracks the incoming cosmic rays and calculates arrival times from light-speed power dynamics, the app broadcasts a high visibility countdown timer and audio alarm across all ship sectors. This gives the crew a critical three-minute window to react before the particles reach the hull. For astronauts working outside the ship, the system sends an automated signal to harden the high-density polymer layer in their suits and activate specialized eye protection. For crew members inside, the app guides them to an easily accessible, insulated safe chamber built from non-radioactive materials. All of this can be very low cost and affordable. It can run on existing crew tablets using free open source software. Meanwhile, the suits and chambers stay affordable by utilizing lightweight commercially available high density polymers.
